verses.text: Therefore, my brothers, whom I love and long for, my joy and crown, that is how you must stand firm in the Lord, my beloved.

xrefs.text: Nevertheless, conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ. Then, whether I come and see you or only hear about you in my absence, I will know that you stand firm in one spirit, contending together as one for the faith of the gospel,
Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong.
Wait patiently for the LORD; be strong and courageous. Wait patiently for the LORD!
as you hold forth the word of life, in order that I may boast on the day of Christ that I did not run or labor in vain.
Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast and immovable. Always excel in the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
Let us hold resolutely to the hope we profess, for He who promised is faithful.

notes.note: Paul uses the word Therefore as a transition word to introduce the exhortations to the Philippian Christians which he is about to give and which are based on the things that he has said before this verse. Consider the best word or phrase to use in your language to show this meaning. Alternate translation: [So then]
See how you translated the word brothers in Philippians 1:12.
Alternate translation: [whom I love and greatly desire to see]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of joy, you can express the idea behind the abstract noun joy by using a verbal form such as “rejoice” or by using an adjective such as “happy.” Alternate translation: [who cause me to be very happy and are my crown]

The phrase my joy and crown could refer to: (1) Paul’s current feelings of joy regarding the Philippian Christians and his future hope of being rewarded for his labor among them. Alternate translation: [my source of joy and my future hope of being rewarded when Christ returns]; (2) Paul’s joy and reward in the future when Christ returns. Alternate translation: [my hope for joy and reward when Christ returns]; (3) Paul’s present joy in the Philippian believers and his present feeling that they are his reward for his work among them. Alternate translation: [my joy and reward]

Paul speaks of the Philippian Christians as if they were his crown. At the time Paul wrote this letter, a crown was made of leaves and was worn by a person on their head as a sign of their achievement after they had won an important victory. Here, the word crown means that the Philippian Christians brought great honor to Paul before God and were a sign of his hard work among them. If your readers would not understand the meaning of this metaphor, you could use an equivalent metaphor from your culture or state the meaning in plain language. Alternate translation: [my reward] or [my honor] or [the sign of my hard work]
Alternate translation: [so continue living for the Lord in the way that I have taught you, dear friends]

The phrase in this way could refer to: (1) what comes before it, in which case this phrase would mean, “in the way that I have just explained to you” Alternate translation: [stand firm in the Lord in the way that I have just explained to you, beloved]; (2) what Paul commands the Philippian Christians to do in Philippians 4:2–9. Alternate translation: [stand firm in the Lord, beloved, in this way]
The phrase stand firm is a command or instruction to all of the Philippian Christians. Use the most natural form in your language to give direction to a group of people.

The phrase stand firm is used to refer to the imagery of a soldier remaining in place, not moved by the enemy. Paul gives this metaphor a spiritual meaning to exhort the Philippian Christians to not change their minds but continue believing what they have already believed. If it would be helpful in your language, consider using another metaphor that would make sense in your culture, or use plain language. Alternate translation: [remain unmoved in your belief in Christ] or [remain firm in your faith]
Alternate translation: [stand firm in your union and relationship with the Lord] or [stand firm in your union and communion with the Lord]

xrefs.text: Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled; do not be afraid.
You will keep in perfect peace the steadfast of mind, because he trusts in You.
Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace at all times and in every way. The Lord be with all of you.
Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, for to this you were called as members of one body. And be thankful.

notes.note: The word and shows that what follows is the result of practicing what comes before and in the previous verse. Alternate translation: [and then]

Paul is using the possessive form to describe a peace that is characterized by having been given by God. If your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express it another way. notes.quote: τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡ ὑπερέχουσα πάντα νοῦν

The phrase which surpasses all understanding could mean: (1) that the peace God gives is so great that human minds are not able to understand it. Alternate translation: [which is greater than we can understand]; (2) that the peace that God gives is superior to anything that humans can contrive through their own efforts. notes.quote: φρουρήσει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν καὶ τὰ νοήματα ὑμῶν
notes.note: The word guard is a military term which refers to a soldier guarding a city or a fortress in order to protect it from enemy attacks. Here Paul presents God’s peace as if it were a soldier who protects hearts and minds from worrying, and so this phrase literally means “will be like a soldier and guard your hearts and minds” or “will be like a soldier standing guard to protect your hearts and minds.” If your readers would not understand this metaphor in this context, you could use an equivalent metaphor from your culture. Alternatively, you could express Paul’s meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will keep your hearts and minds safe from attacks of worry and fear] or [will keep your hearts and minds safe] or [will protect your hearts and minds]

verses.text: Nevertheless, you have done well to share in my affliction.

xrefs.text: And do not neglect to do good and to share with others, for with such sacrifices God is pleased.
It is right for me to feel this way about all of you, since I have you in my heart. For in my chains and in my defense and confirmation of the gospel, you are all partners in grace with me.
You sympathized with those in prison and joyfully accepted the confiscation of your property, knowing that you yourselves had a better and permanent possession.
But the LORD said to my father David, ‘Since it was in your heart to build a house for My Name, you have done well to have this in your heart.
Nevertheless, the one who receives instruction in the word must share in all good things with his instructor.
His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!
Instruct them to do good, to be rich in good works, and to be generous and ready to share,
I have all I need and more, now that I have received your gifts from Epaphroditus. They are a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God.

notes.note: The phrase having shared together in my affliction means that the Philippian believers helped Paul while he was experiencing difficulties by giving him money and sending Epaphroditus to him. If it would help your readers, you could state this explicitly. Alternate translation: [by helping me in my affliction through your gift of money and sending Epaphroditus to me] or [by helping me when I faced difficult circumstances by sending Epaphroditus to encourage me and bring me your gift of money]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of affliction, you can express the idea behind the abstract noun affliction with an adjective such as difficult or in some other way. Alternate translation: [when I was suffering] or [when I was mistreated]
Alternate translation: [in my trials] or [in my troubles] or [in my difficulties]

verses.text: And as you Philippians know, in the early days of the gospel, when I left Macedonia, no church but you partnered with me in the matter of giving and receiving.

xrefs.text: because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now,
I robbed other churches by accepting their support in order to serve you.
After Paul and Silas came out of the prison, they went to Lydia’s house to see the brothers and encourage them. Then they left the city.
I have become a fool, but you drove me to it. In fact, you should have commended me, since I am in no way inferior to those “super-apostles, even though I am nothing.

notes.note: Here, in the beginning of the gospel refers to when Paul first began communicating the gospel message to the Philippians. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state explicitly the idea behind this phrase. Alternate translation: [when you first heard me preach the gospel]
See how you translated the phrase the gospel in Philippians 1:5 and 4:3.

notes.quote: οὐδεμία μοι ἐκκλησία ἐκοινώνησεν εἰς λόγον δόσεως καὶ λήμψεως, εἰ μὴ ὑμεῖς μόνοι
notes.note: You can state no church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving except you alone in the positive. Alternate translation: [you were the only church that shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving]
Here, shared with me means the Philippians helped Paul financially and in other practical ways. Alternate translation: [were partners with] or [helped me]

In the original language in which Paul wrote this letter, the phrase giving and receiving could refer either to exchanges that involved money or to exchanges that involved the giving and receiving of non-financial things that would benefit the other party. Here, the phrase giving and receiving may refer to both financial and non-financial gifts because the Philippians helped Paul by sending a gift of money via Epaphroditus, who also helped Paul in other ways. Alternate translation: [by sending money and help to me]

named.name: Philippi
named.brief: A city in Macedonia visited by Paul

named.name: Macedonia
named.brief: A region in northern Greece; Paul preached there

verses.text: For even while I was in Thessalonica, you provided for my needs again and again.

xrefs.text: Surely you recall, brothers, our labor and toil. We worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to anyone while we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.
When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
For we wanted to come to you— indeed I, Paul, tried again and again— but Satan obstructed us.

notes.note: Alternate translation: [for even when I was in Thessalonica]

The phrase both once and twice is an idiom meaning that something occurred more than one time. If your readers would not understand this idiom, you could use an equivalent idiom from your language, or you could state this in plain language. Alternate translation: [several times]

Paul is leaving out some of the words that this phrase would need in many languages to be complete. If it would be clearer in your language, you could supply these words from the context. Alternate translation: [you sent me money to help me with my needs]

named.name: Thessalonica
named.brief: Macedonian city, site of an early Christian church

verses.text: Not that I am seeking a gift, but I am looking for the fruit that may be credited to your account.

xrefs.text: And our people must also learn to devote themselves to good works in order to meet the pressing needs of others, so that they will not be unfruitful.
For God is not unjust. He will not forget your work and the love you have shown for His name as you have ministered to the saints and continue to do so.
As it is written: “He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever.”
This is to My Father’s glory, that you bear much fruit, proving yourselves to be My disciples.

So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to visit you beforehand and make arrangements for the generous gift you had promised. This way, your gift will be prepared generously and not begrudgingly.
As God’s steward, an overseer must be above reproach— not self-willed, not quick-tempered, not given to drunkenness, not violent, not greedy for money.
Be shepherds of God’s flock that is among you, watching over them not out of compulsion, but willingly, as God would have you; not out of greed, but out of eagerness;
You did not choose Me, but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit— fruit that will remain— so that whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.

notes.quote: ἐπιζητῶ τὸν καρπὸν τὸν πλεονάζοντα εἰς λόγον ὑμῶν
notes.note: At the time Paul wrote this letter, the word fruit could be used in a business context to refer to what was gained in a financial transaction. When used in a business context, the word fruit meant “profit” or “gain.” Here Paul is using this business meaning to refer to God’s reward. If your language has an equivalent word that could be used in a business context, consider using it here if it would be natural in your language. Alternately, you may express this meaning using plain language, as the UST does. Alternate translation: [I seek the profit that increases to your account] or [I seek the gain that increases to your account]

verses.text: I have all I need and more, now that I have received your gifts from Epaphroditus. They are a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God.

xrefs.text: And do not neglect to do good and to share with others, for with such sacrifices God is pleased.
For this ministry of service is not only supplying the needs of the saints but is also overflowing in many expressions of thanksgiving to God.
I know how to live humbly, and I know how to abound. In any and every situation I have learned the secret of being filled and being hungry, of having plenty and having need.
and walk in love, just as Christ loved us and gave Himself up for us as a fragrant sacrificial offering to God.
But I thought it necessary to send back to you Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier, who is also your messenger and minister to my needs.
But thanks be to God, who always leads us triumphantly as captives in Christ and through us spreads everywhere the fragrance of the knowledge of Him.
Therefore I urge you, brothers, on account of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.
We are obligated to thank God for you all the time, brothers, as is fitting, because your faith is growing more and more, and your love for one another is increasing.

notes.note: The phrase I have all things in full could mean: (1) that Paul has received all things that he needs from the Philippian believers and is therefore sufficiently supplied. Alternate translation: [I have everything I need and am content]; (2) that Paul is continuing the business metaphor from Philippians 4:17 and is here offering the Philippians a figurative receipt for the gifts they gave him. Alternate translation: [I have received the gift that you sent]

The phrase I abound means that Paul has more than enough of the things that he needs for himself. If it would be helpful in your language, consider stating this explicitly. Alternate translation: [I have more than enough of the things I need]

notes.quote: πεπλήρωμαι, δεξάμενος παρὰ Ἐπαφροδίτου τὰ παρ’ ὑμῶν
notes.note: Connecting Statement: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express the phrase I have been filled with an active form, and you could state who did the action. Alternate translation: [You have fully provided for me by giving me the things which Epaphroditus brought to me]
Epaphroditus is the name of a man. See how you translated his name in Philippians 2:25.

notes.quote: ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, θυσίαν δεκτήν, εὐάρεστον τῷ Θεῷ
notes.note: Here Paul speaks of the gift from the Philippian believers as if it were a sacrifice offered to God on an altar. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this phrase by stating the meaning using plain language. Alternate translation: [which are very pleasing to God] or [which make God happy] or [which I assure you are gifts very pleasing to God, like an acceptable sacrifice]

named.name: Epaphroditus
named.brief: A messenger and minister to Paul from Philippi.

verses.text: And my God will supply all your needs according to His glorious riches in Christ Jesus.

xrefs.text: And God is able to make all grace abound to you, so that in all things, at all times, having all that you need, you will abound in every good work.
For the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives grace and glory; He withholds no good thing from those who walk with integrity.
And after you have suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, who has called you to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore you, secure you, strengthen you, and establish you.
Instruct those who are rich in the present age not to be conceited and not to put their hope in the uncertainty of wealth, but in God, who richly provides all things for us to enjoy.
A Psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
But as for me, I will look to the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your crops;

He humbled you, and in your hunger He gave you manna to eat, which neither you nor your fathers had known, so that you might understand that man does not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.

notes.note: The word for will fulfill is the same word translated as “have been fulfilled” in verse 18. This phrase is an idiom meaning “will provide everything you need”

notes.quote: κατὰ τὸ πλοῦτος αὐτοῦ ἐν δόξῃ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ
notes.note: Alternate translation: [from his glorious riches that he gives through Christ Jesus]

named.name: Jesus
named.brief: The Son of God and Savior of the world.

verses.text: To our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.

xrefs.text: For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever! Amen.
Not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to Your name be the glory, because of Your loving devotion, because of Your faithfulness.
And he said in a loud voice, “Fear God and give Him glory, because the hour of His judgment has come. Worship the One who made the heavens and the earth and the sea and the springs of waters.
saying, “Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom and thanks and honor and power and strength be to our God forever and ever! Amen.
And blessed be His glorious name forever; may all the earth be filled with His glory. Amen and amen.
In a loud voice they were saying: “Worthy is the Lamb who was slain, to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing!
filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
to the only God our Savior be glory, majesty, dominion, and authority through Jesus Christ our Lord before all time, and now, and for all eternity. Amen.

notes.note: When Paul says our, he is speaking of himself and the Philippian believers, so our is inclusive. Your language may require you to mark this form.

verses.text: Greet all the saints in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me send you greetings.

xrefs.text: and all the brothers with me, To the churches of Galatia:
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, To the saints in Ephesus, the faithful in Christ Jesus:
Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, To all the saints in Christ Jesus at Philippi, together with the overseers and deacons:
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings,
Timothy, my fellow worker, sends you greetings, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my fellow countrymen.
To the church of God in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy, together with all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:
My fellow prisoner Aristarchus sends you greetings, as does Mark the cousin of Barnabas. You have already received instructions about him: If he comes to you, welcome him.
Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,

notes.note: Greet is a command or instruction to all of the Philippian Christians. Use the most natural form in your language to give direction to a group of people.

See how you translated the word brothers in Philippians 1:12. Paul is using the term brothers here to refer to anyone who is a fellow believer in Jesus. If this is not clear in your language, you could express this plainly. Alternate translation: [My fellow believers here]

See how you translated the word brothers in Philippians 1:12. Although the term brothers is masculine, Paul is using the word here in a spiritual sense to include both men and women who believe in Jesus. Alternate translation: [The brothers and sisters with me]

named.name: Jesus
named.brief: The Son of God and Savior of the world.

verses.text: All the saints send you greetings, especially those from the household of Caesar.

xrefs.text: As a result, it has become clear throughout the whole palace guard and to everyone else that I am in chains for Christ.
All the saints send you greetings.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ send you greetings.
The church in Babylon, chosen together with you, sends you greetings, as does my son Mark.
But Ananias answered, “Lord, many people have told me about this man and all the harm he has done to Your saints in Jerusalem.
Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy send you greetings.

notes.note: The phrase the household of Caesar refers to the servants who worked in Caesar’s palace.

verses.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.

xrefs.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.
The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

notes.note: Paul describes the Philippian Christians as whole persons by reference to their spirit. Alternate translation: [be with you]

notes.quote: ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματος ὑμῶν
notes.note: The word grace is an abstract noun that can be translated with an adverb. Alternate translation: [May the Lord Jesus Christ act graciously to you]

named.name: LORD
named.brief: Names or title used to refer to God

named.brief: The Son of God and Savior of the world.
